extracted.intended_audience: repository managers, metadata providers, data curators, librarians, and implementers who supply or integrate repository metadata into OpenAIRE
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidelines for harvesting, classifying, and ingesting metadata and links about scholarly outputs (literature, datasets, software, other research products) into the OpenAIRE graph. Covers scope, quality, mapping rules, handling of full-text and accessioned datasets, and required agreements (ToU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of harvested content (product types and sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenAIRE service infrastructure harvests metadata about scholarly communication products (literature, datasets, software, and other research products) and links between such products from a range of institutional or subject repositories, national and institutional research information portals, aggregators, e-journals, data repositories, and software repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OpenAIRE also infers links between literature and such products via advanced text and data mining techniques (TDM). The resulting information graph is intended to favour monitoring of open science and open science publishing workflows (e.g. science reproducibility and transparent assessment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAIRE will actively pursue harvesting content from European but also non-European repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage is not restricted to Europe; policy emphasises active pursuit of both European and non-European sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / interlinking objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenAIRE graph aims at interlinking research outcomes (citations, mentions, references) and also with the research entities (people, organisations, services, facilities) that generate or use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications have a special role as they are linked with all products used or resulting in the relative research activity; this supports monitoring reproducibility and transparent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication cadence of the OpenAIRE graph
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAIRE publishes every 6 months the graph in Zenodo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The graph is periodically released (biannually) to enable external access and re-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring: linking to funders, projects, and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenAIRE graph links research products with the funders and projects resulting from their grants and includes affiliation links to allow monitoring at institutional level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking to funders/projects and affiliations enables monitoring and reporting at project and institutional granularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community linkage (multi-community view)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OpenAIRE graph links research products with the communities for which they are relevant, in order to provide a (multi-)community-view of the scholarly output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items are associated with research communities to support community-specific discovery and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control of data sources and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sources and repositories are quality-controlled: their metadata respects the OpenAIRE guidelines and their import in OpenAIRE is curated by OpenAIRE data curators with the support of the OpenAIRE Metadata Validator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repositories must supply metadata that conforms to OpenAIRE guidelines; ingestion is curated and validated by OpenAIRE tooling and curators. A registry of current data sources is available (link referenced on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of Use / legal consent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sources and repositories accept a ToU with OpenAIRE (and viceversa) to re-use data under specific consent, warranties, and license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repositories must accept the ToU governing OpenAIRE’s reuse of harvested metadata and any permitted uses of collected full-texts (see OpenAIRE ToU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion: metadata structure and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAIRE accepts the metadata records of all scientific products whose structure respect the model and semantics as expressed by the OpenAIRE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both Open Access and non-Open Access material will be included; links to other products will be resolved where possible (i.e. the provided PIDs have a resolver). If metadata does not conform to the model/semantics, it will not be accepted until corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: PID resolvability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to other products will be resolved where this is possible (i.e. the provided PIDs have a resolver).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enable link resolution inside the graph, repositories should provide persistent identifiers (PIDs) that resolve; unresolved or non-resolving PIDs limit linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of datasets with accession numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets with accession numbers (database entries) are not included as OpenAIRE datasets but, when a relationship to product exists, are included as properties of the related products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, they are included as values of the property externalReference of product metadata; externalReference includes a URL to the splash page, the target web site name, the ID and an ID type (e.g. PDB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-text of scientific literature: harvesting and use
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAIRE collects Open Access literature product files whenever these are accessible from the URL provided in the metadata record. The literature full-text is used for text-mining purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End-users cannot download full-text files from OpenAIRE; they are forwarded to the original source of deposition. Use of full-texts is governed by OpenAIRE’s ToU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation: repository categories and need for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAIRE services collect metadata about four typologies of products: literature, datasets, software, and 'other research products' (ORPs). Metadata can be collected from four main categories of repositories: literature repositories, data repositories, software repositories, and ORP repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is not a one-to-one relationship between repository category and contained product types; aggregation must classify products collected from a repository to assign them to the correct OpenAIRE entity class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping vocabularies and standards used for distribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution rules follow vocabularies in the OpenAIRE guidelines and Version 4.0 of DataCite. Such mappings may be modified over time to reflect the preferences and requirements of the OpenAIRE user community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should consult the current mappings (links provided on the page) because mappings are continuously updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for literature repositories: mapping of resource types
rubrics_metrics.description: For literature repositories (publishers, journals, institutional/thematic repositories, aggregators, catalogues) resource types are mapped to OpenAIRE entities: resource types not associated to Dataset/Software/Other => Literature; resource types indicating datasets, image, video, audio => Dataset; resource types indicating software => Software; resource types indicating other research products (e.g. 'Service', 'Interactive Resource', 'Other') => ORP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository-provided resource type vocabularies must be interpreted/mapped according to these rules to assign each record to the correct OpenAIRE entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for data repositories: mapping of resource types
rubrics_metrics.description: For data repositories (data repositories, aggregators) mapping rules include: resource type indicating papers (based on repository-specific vocabularies) => Literature; resource types different from ones associated to Literature/Software/Other => Dataset; resource types indicating software => Software; resource types indicating other research products => ORP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in data repositories, records that indicate papers must be classed as literature; repository vocabularies must be mapped accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for software repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: For software repositories: all records are mapped to Software (none mapped to Literature, Dataset, or ORP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software repositories are treated as containing only software products for the purpose of OpenAIRE entity assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for other research product (ORP) repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: For other research product repositories: all records are mapped to ORP (none to Literature, Dataset, or Software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repositories identified as 'other product repositories' will have all records classified as 'Other research product'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation process: term-to-entity mapping using common vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently from the category of input repository, the aggregation process identifies for each input record a term in a common vocabulary. Each term of this vocabulary is then associated to one of the four OpenAIRE entities: literature, dataset, software, and ORP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mappings between specific types of products and the target OpenAIRE entities are specified by dedicated vocabularies that are continuously updated; implementers must map repository-specific terms to the common vocabulary before ingestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research product 'Literature' example mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of terms mapped to the OpenAIRE 'Literature' entity include: Article (0001), Book (0002), Conference Object (0004), Contribution for newspaper or weekly magazine (0005), Doctoral Thesis (0006), Master Thesis (0007), Bachelor Thesis (0008), External Research Report (0009), Internal report (0011), Newsletter (0012), Part of book or chapter of book (0013), Research (0014), Review (0015), Preprint (0016), Report (0017), Patent (0019), Data Paper (0031), Software Paper (0032), Project deliverable (0034), Project milestone (0035), Project proposal (0036), Other literature type (0038).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current, up-to-date mapping is available at the OpenAIRE vocabulary endpoint referenced on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research product 'Dataset' example mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of terms mapped to 'Dataset' include: Dataset (0021), Film (0024), Image (0025), Sound (0030), Audiovisual (0033), Clinical Trial (0037), Other dataset type (0039).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the OpenAIRE dataset typologies vocabulary for authoritative and updated lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research product 'Software' example mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of terms mapped to 'Software' include: Software (0029) and Other software type (0040).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software-related records should use these terms in the common vocabulary mapping to be assigned to the Software entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research product 'Other research product (ORP)' example mappings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of terms mapped to ORP include: Lecture (0010), Annotation (0018), Event (0023), Interactive Resource (0026), Model (0027), Physical Object (0028), Other ORP type (0020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records representing these types should be mapped to 'Other research product' in the aggregation process; vocabulary endpoint provides the up-to-date list.
